question:
Now we need to determine 4 out of 5 workers to each complete one of the four tasks. Since each worker has different skill sets, the amount of time required for each worker to complete each task is also different. The time required for each worker to complete each task is shown in Table 5-2.
Table 5-2
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline Task Time Required & $A$ & $B$ & $C$ & $D$ \\
\hline Worker & & & & \\
\hline I & 9 & 4 & 3 & 7 \\
\hline II & 4 & 6 & 5 & 6 \\
\hline III & 5 & 4 & 7 & 5 \\
\hline IV & 7 & 5 & 2 & 3 \\
\hline V & 10 & 6 & 7 & 4 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

Try to find a work assignment plan that minimizes the total working hours.

    },

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.W = pyo.Set(initialize=d["workers"], ordered=True)
    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=d["tasks"], ordered=True)

    # Variables: x[i,j] = 1 if worker i is assigned to task j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.W, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimise total working hours
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["time"][i][j] * m.x[i, j] for i in m.W for j in m.T)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Each task is completed by exactly one worker
    def task_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for i in m.W) == 1

    model.task_assign = pyo.Constraint(model.T, rule=task_rule)

    # Each worker does at most one task
    def worker_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for j in m.T) <= d["max_tasks_per_worker"]

    model.worker_assign = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=worker_rule)

    return model

"""
Assignment problem: assign 4 of 5 workers to 4 tasks (A, B, C, D), one worker per task,
one task per worker, minimizing total working hours.

Decision variables:
    x[i, j] in {0,1}  -- 1 if worker i is assigned to task j, else 0.
        index sets: i in WORKERS = {I, II, III, IV, V}, j in TASKS = {A, B, C, D}

Objective (minimize):
    total working hours = sum_{i,j} time[i,j] * x[i,j]

Constraints:
    (1) Each task j is done by exactly one worker:  sum_i x[i,j] = 1   for all j
    (2) Each worker i does at most one task:        sum_j x[i,j] <= 1  for all i
        (the "at most" allows exactly one worker to be left unassigned, i.e. 4 of 5)
"""

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=d["workers"])      # workers
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=d["tasks"])        # tasks
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=[(i, j) for i in d["workers"] for j in d["tasks"]],
                      dimen=2)

    # x[i,j] = 1 if worker i is assigned task j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # y[i] = 1 if worker i is used at all

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["time"][(i, j)] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in m.P)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    def task_done_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for i in m.I) == 1
    model.task_once = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=task_done_rule)

    # (c) worker "used" indicator equals number of tasks assigned (0 or 1)
    def worker_usage_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for j in m.J) == m.y[i]
    model.worker_usage = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=worker_usage_rule)

    def count_workers_rule(m):
        return sum(m.y[i] for i in m.I) == d["num_tasks"]
    model.count_workers = pyo.Constraint(rule=count_workers_rule)

    return model
